key_insight: Square unfolding of symmetric spiked tensors has a sharp partial-recovery transition at λ ≍ n^((p−2)/4), with spectral behavior resembling Wigner matrices after symmetry-dependent transformations.
engineering_relevance: The results clarify the signal-strength scaling needed for spectral recovery from symmetric tensor data without approximating dependent noise entries as independent.
method: Analyze symmetric Gaussian tensor noise directly using random matrix theory.
Derive limiting spectra, deterministic equivalents, recovery thresholds and signal overlaps.
Extend the analysis to orthogonal spikes, recursive unfolding and non-square unfolding.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical asymptotic results validating a 2014 conjecture by Montanari and Richard, but describes no empirical benchmarks.
watch_item: The recovery guarantees are asymptotic under symmetric Gaussian noise; the proposed square-versus-long unfolding tradeoff remains conjectural.
paper_title: A Random Matrix Analysis of Symmetric Tensor Unfolding
